image_description: A close-up, high-resolution profile view of a Nile crocodile's head against a stark black background. The image highlights the textured, armored skin (osteoderms), the dorsal positioning of the eye with a visible vertical slit pupil, and the massive jawline with interlocking conical teeth. The snout tapers towards the right, showing the characteristic V-shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The profile clearly shows a tapering, V-shaped snout distinct from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad at the base.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The jawline is thick and robust. Multiple conical teeth are visible along the margin, appearing to interlock correctly without fusion or melting artifacts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is located on the top ridge of the skull (dorsal). A clear vertical slit pupil is visible. The surrounding eyelid structure suggests the presence of a nictitating membrane mechanism, though the membrane itself isn't fully deployed, which is normal for a static pose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped such that the very tip of the snout where nostrils would be located is outside the frame or obscured by the angle/lighting. Cannot verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While only the head/neck is visible, the transition to the neck shows heavy armor plating consistent with an elongated, armored body plan.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing distinct, raised bony scutes with a rough, irregular pattern typical of crocodilian osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration matches the description (earthy browns/greys) and the texture is visibly rough and non-uniform.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image focuses on the dorsal and lateral aspects of the head. The ventral (belly) scales are not visible in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is not visible in the image.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification of species-level features (snout shape, tooth arrangement, scale texture) to distinguish from alligators or other crocodilians.
To detect subtle AI artifacts in the complex, high-frequency texture of the osteoderms and potential edge bleeding against the black background.
To ensure the complex geometry of the jaw and eye sockets forms a coherent, watertight mesh without floating fragments or internal holes.

focus_areas: Integrity of the eye structure (pupil shape and eyelid connection)
Continuity of the jawline and tooth roots (no melting/fusion)
Consistency of scale patterns (osteoderms) across lighting gradients
Edge sharpness against the black background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'interlocking' nature of the teeth. AI often fails to render the specific notch in the upper jaw for the 4th lower tooth. Verify if the teeth look like individual solid objects or if they merge into the gum line. Also, check the eye reflection; it should be consistent with a single light source given the high contrast.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
